name: Unity
description: Agents build your game in the Unity editor on this computer, through Unity's Pipeline package: Genex makes or sets up the game's Unity project and opens it in your Unity 6. The project lives in the game's own folder. Unity is a trademark or registered trademark of Unity Technologies or its affiliates.

tools.name: new-game
tools.description: Make this game's Unity project: an empty project in this game's folder as unity/, for the newest Unity 6 installed here, with Unity's Pipeline package, the standard built-in modules (physics, audio, animation, UI…) and the UI package. Genex opens it in Unity and waits until the editor answers, so the unity-editor tools reach it. Use it only when the user chose Unity for this game and it has no Unity project yet; a game that already holds one, or has something named unity, is refused. A first start takes a minute or two while Unity imports the project and downloads its packages.

tools.name: show-steps
tools.description: Show the user the Unity setup card in this game's chat: Genex installs Unity Hub and Unity 6 for them, and they only sign in to Unity. Use it when the user wants a Unity game and this computer has no Unity 6 yet (new-game refuses, or the engine question says Unity needs installing first); then tell them in one line and end your reply, and the chat tells you when Unity is ready. It does nothing when Unity 6 is installed and signed in.

tools.name: multiplayer
tools.description: Make this Unity game playable online with Genex multiplayer, in its WebGL build and its Mac and Windows builds alike (web and native players meet in the same rooms): embeds Genex's package (Packages/com.genex.multiplayer), asks for the Colyseus Unity SDK it runs on in Packages/manifest.json, writes Assets/Genex/link.xml, Assets/Genex/GenexGame.cs (GenexGame.Slug: the game's Genex project from Genex's Play, the published page or GenexSettings.json, so builds made before the first publish join once published) and the game's Genex project in Assets/Resources/GenexSettings.json, and its matchmaking in genex.json. Its package holds both the relay client and the server-authoritative room client. Call it once when the person wants people to play together, then read the unity-multiplayer skill and write the online play (the relay, or a server room for competitive play); call it again with slug after the first publish only to test online in the editor or a build started by hand. Never add npm or a package.json for this.

matchmaking.description: How players are matched, as Genex reads it at publish: {"preset": "open" | "duel" | "arena" | "teams" | "private", "winCondition"?: "lastStanding" | "firstToScore" | "highScoreInTime" | "firstToFinish", "config"?: {"minPlayers": 2, "maxPlayers": 10, …}}. Leave it out to keep the game's current matchmaking.

slug.description: The game's Genex project (genex__publish-status names it after the first publish), for the editor and builds started by hand; Genex's Play and the published page name it to the others. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

tools.name: setup
tools.description: Set this game's existing Unity project up for Genex, once the user confirms: adds Unity's Pipeline package to its Packages/manifest.json (everything else stays; a copy of the manifest is kept), then opens the project in the Unity it was saved with unless Unity already has it open. Use it when a unity-editor call says the project has no Pipeline package. A project older than Unity 6 is refused.
tools.confirmation: Set this Unity project up for Genex: add Unity's Pipeline package to its Packages/manifest.json, which lets agents work in its open editor, and open the project in Unity. Genex keeps a copy of the manifest first.

tools.name: undo-setup
tools.description: Take back what setup added to this game's Unity project, once the user confirms: the Pipeline package's line in Packages/manifest.json, only while it is still as Genex wrote it. Use it only when the user asks.
tools.confirmation: Take back what Genex added to this Unity project: the Pipeline package's line in its Packages/manifest.json. Anything else you changed stays, and agents can no longer reach its editor.

tools.name: open-editor
tools.description: Open this game's Unity project in the Unity it was saved with and wait until the editor answers. Use it when a unity-editor call says the project is not open. It opens nothing when Unity already has the project open, and never opens it in another Unity version.

tools.name: restart-editor
tools.description: End this game's Unity editor and open its project again, once the user confirms. Use it only when unity-editor calls keep saying Unity's main thread ran nothing (a dialog nobody answered, or the editor hangs) and waiting did not help; to close Unity, call quit-editor instead. While Unity still answers, Genex stops its play and saves its scenes and assets first; a stalled editor can't save, and its unsaved work is lost, so say what will be lost first. Genex never restarts Unity by itself: the user confirms each restart.
tools.confirmation: End Unity and open this game's project again. Use this when Unity stopped answering, for example behind a dialog. Work you have not saved in the editor is lost.

tools.name: quit-editor
tools.description: Save this game's open Unity editor (each scene with unsaved work by its path, then its assets; the agent's own play is stopped first), then quit Unity. Use it when Unity must be closed, or the user asks. It never quits an editor whose work it couldn't save (a scene that has no file yet, a save Unity refused, an editor that doesn't answer, the user's own play) and says why. Open it again with open-editor.

tools.name: find-project
tools.description: For Genex only: finds the Unity project in this game's folder (the folder holding ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt: the game's own, else unity/, else the first by path) and keeps it for the editor connector.

tools.name: engine-status
tools.description: For Genex's chat only: whether this computer has a Unity 6 Genex makes projects with (ready), only an older Unity (older-only) or none (none), its version, and the words the engine question offers Unity with.

tools.name: save-all
tools.description: For Genex only: saves this game's open Unity editor before Genex snapshots or restores the game's files: each scene with unsaved work by its own path, then changed assets and settings. A scene that was never saved is never saved for it (Unity would ask for its file name in a dialog).

tools.name: end-editor
tools.description: For Genex only: ends this game's Unity editor before a restore puts other files under it, saving nothing (save-all runs first), and remembers it did so it is opened again afterwards.

tools.name: reopen-editor
tools.description: For Genex only: opens this game's Unity project again after a restore that closed it.

tools.name: editor-state
tools.description: For Genex only: whether this game's Unity editor answers: quiet when it does, pending while it starts, reloads or imports, failed when it is gone or its main thread ran nothing for two minutes.

tools.name: after-run
tools.description: For Genex only: at a run's end, starts the idle time of a Unity editor Genex's agent opened, after which Genex may close it.

tools.name: scene-shots
tools.description: For Genex only: the main camera's still of this game's open scene, as an image, for a run's save point and for the reviewer of its finish.

tools.name: editor-activity
tools.description: For Genex only: whether the person is using this game's Unity editor (it plays a game the agent did not start, and agents may not use Unity while the person plays) and how many open scenes have unsaved work; the editor lock's probe.

tools.name: play-open
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: start this project's Unity Play mode or join its running play. Requires an active Input System package; no packages are installed or changed. Answers {width,height,joined}; fresh refuses a person's play.

fresh.description: True: start the play over from the game's start (a play an agent left running is ended first; the person's is never touched).

tools.name: play-input
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: move the player's relative mouse or wheel for one frame, then hold keys or aimed mouse buttons together for game seconds and release them. Requires Unity's Input System; legacy input injection is not supported. Answers {held,gameSeconds}.

keys.description: Web key codes or mouse buttons (MouseLeft, MouseRight, MouseMiddle) held together, joined by commas: KeyW,ShiftLeft (empty: just let the game play).

seconds.description: Game seconds to hold them, 0.05 to 10.

dx.description: Pixels of mouse motion to the right for one frame first (negative: left).

dy.description: Pixels of mouse motion down the screen for one frame first (negative: up).

wheel.description: Notches of the mouse wheel for one frame first, up positive.

tools.name: play-shot
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: capture the running Game view, including its HUD, as {png (base64),width,height}.

tools.name: play-state
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: read the running game's clock and the Player-tagged object's transform, when present.

tools.name: play-pause
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: set paused true to freeze Unity Play mode, or false to resume it. Repeating the same value leaves it unchanged.

paused.description: True stands the game still; false lets it run.

tools.name: play-close
tools.description: For Genex's computer tool only: end the play this session started, or restore a joined play's original pause and runtime background settings. Answers {closed}.

skills.name: unity-multiplayer
skills.summary: Genex multiplayer for this Unity game, WebGL and native builds alike: unity__multiplayer sets it up, then the relay (GenexMultiplayer) or, for competitive play, a server-authoritative room (server/room.ts, GenexAuthority.Connect, genex__room). MANDATORY before any online or multiplayer code.

skills.name: unity-editor
skills.summary: How to build this Unity game in the person's open editor: the unity-editor commands, C# scripts and recompiles, .meta files, scenes and prefabs changed and saved through commands, run_script for levels, captures, packages and builds.

settings.label: Close Unity 15 minutes after a run when Genex opened it for that run and nobody used it since

mcpServers.description: The user's open Unity editor through Unity's Pipeline package on 127.0.0.1: its own commands for scenes, objects, assets, prefabs, materials, Play mode, captures, tests and settings. Each game's calls go to the Unity project in its own folder, while the user has that project open in Unity with the Pipeline package (com.unity.pipeline) added.
